title: Better than Random: Reliable NLG Human Evaluation with Constrained Active Sampling
research_question: Can a constrained active sampling procedure select a limited human-evaluation subset that preserves full-dataset NLG system rankings more reliably than random or heuristic sampling?
methodology: The authors propose Constrained Active Sampling Framework (CASF), which iteratively combines a learner that predicts sample quality, systematic sampling across predicted quality levels, and a constrained controller intended to reduce redundancy. They re-evaluate 137 NLG evaluation setups involving 137 systems, 44 human-evaluation metrics, 16 datasets, and five NLG task types. Subset-derived system rankings are compared with rankings on the full datasets using Kendall's Tau, with additional tests for top-system identification and retention of statistically significant system differences. CASF is compared with random sampling, heuristic sampling, and several ablations, with additional analyses across sampling ratios, sample sizes, preliminary automatic metrics, and phase configurations.

key_findings.finding: Repeated random sampling can produce materially different inter-system rankings, with 87.5% of examined datasets showing different rankings across five random samples.
At the main 50% sampling setting, CASF achieved an overall inter-system ranking Kendall correlation of 0.83, exceeding the reported aggregate performance of the comparison methods.
key_findings.section: Results and Analysis / Full Inter-System Ranking Accuracy

key_findings.finding: CASF ranked first on 79.55% of the 44 human-evaluation metrics and first or second on 90.91% of them.
key_findings.section: Results and Analysis / Full Inter-System Ranking Accuracy

key_findings.finding: CASF identified the full-dataset top-ranked system correctly for 93.18% of the 44 human-evaluation metrics.
key_findings.section: Results and Analysis / Top-Ranked System Accuracy

key_findings.finding: Wilcoxon signed-rank comparisons reported statistically better ranking performance for CASF than random and heuristic sampling.
key_findings.section: Results and Analysis / Full Inter-System Ranking Accuracy

key_findings.finding: CASF generally retained inter-system ranking accuracy better than random and heuristic sampling over a range of sampling ratios and typical fixed sample sizes, although individual dataset and sampling-ratio cases did not always favor CASF.
key_findings.section: Appendix / Different Sampling Ratio; Different Sampling Size

key_findings.finding: For preserving statistically significant pairwise system differences at a 50% sample rate, CASF obtained slightly higher retention accuracy than random and heuristic sampling at both the 0.05 and 0.001 significance levels.

Among the automatic metrics tested for preliminary sample-quality ordering, MOVER-SCORE produced the strongest average pre-ranking result, while the authors found five sampling phases effective in most tested cases.
key_findings.section: Results and Analysis / Automatic Metric for Preliminary Phase; Phases and Associated Sampling Ratios

limitations: CASF predicts sample quality from automatic-metric features, which the authors acknowledge may not comprehensively represent sample quality.
The redundancy controller also uses a limited representation of sample similarity, and the authors suggest incorporating additional characteristics in future work.
The empirical study is restricted to NLG human evaluation, so applicability to other NLP evaluation tasks is not established.
The learner requires enough labeled samples for training, and the authors state that CASF may not be appropriate for extremely small evaluation samples, such as fewer than 50 items.
CASF does not dominate the baselines for every individual dataset and sampling ratio.
Its primary target is reliable system ranking from already available human scores rather than direct evaluation of factual correctness, evidence attribution, or omissions in generated content.
raw_claims: Human evaluation on different sampled subsets can yield different rankings of the same NLG systems.
Random sampling produced different system rankings across repeated draws for most datasets examined.
CASF selects samples through a learner, a systematic sampler, and a redundancy-constraining controller.
Previously annotated samples are used to update the learner during later active-sampling phases.
Ranking quality is evaluated by comparing subset-derived and full-dataset system rankings with Kendall's Tau.
The main evaluation covers 44 human-evaluation metrics across 16 datasets and five NLG task families.
CASF achieved 93.18% accuracy at recognizing the top-ranked system.
CASF ranked first or second on 90.91% of the evaluated human metrics.
MOVER-SCORE was the strongest tested automatic metric for the preliminary quality-ranking stage.
CASF generally performed better as the available sampling ratio increased, although non-monotonic cases occurred.
CASF slightly improved retention of statistically significant differences between systems relative to random and heuristic sampling.
The method can be unsuitable when the available sample size is too small to train its learner.
